thread:
Ben Carter: Kicking off the Lifecycle Growth Experiments sprint (activation + early retention) 🚀

Goals for this sprint:
- Lift activation (first successful production-like inference call) within 24h/72h
- Improve D7/D14 retention for self-serve devs

We’re running 3 levers in parallel:
1) Onboarding email sequences (welcome/quickstart/first-success/troubleshooting/next step)
2) In-console nudges (setup checklist + contextual banners + JIT prompts)
3) Retargeting for non-activated + recently lapsed (LinkedIn/Google)

Working links (latest):
- PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PROD/lifecycle-growth-experiments-sprint
- Experiment tracker (Drive): https://drive.google.com/redwood/gtm/experiment-tracker
- Email copy v1 (Drive): https://drive.google.com/redwood/gtm/onboarding-email-copy-v1
- Retargeting creative brief (Drive): https://drive.google.com/redwood/gtm/retargeting-creative-brief

Owners:
- Email sequence: Ben + Soojin (messaging review) + Tyler (ops + suppression)
- Retargeting: Ben + Soojin + Ethan (benchmark proof points) + Tessa (creative direction)
- Console nudges: Marissa/Paula (PM) + Design (Kenji/Alicia) + we’ll coordinate messaging from marketing side

Timeline (target):
- Week 0 (this week): tracking + final copy/creative + QA
- Week 1: launch v1 (email + console nudge v1 + retargeting audiences)
- Week 2: iterate (A/B variants + fixes)
- Week 3: readout + decision

Review deadlines (so we actually ship):
- Email copy v1 final: Fri 1/17 EOD PT
- Retargeting concept 1st pass: Mon 1/20 noon PT
- UTM + attribution naming locked: Tue 1/21

Reply here w/ any blockers + confirm you’re good w/ deadlines.

(reactions: :rocket: x6 :eyes: x3)

Tyler Benson: Confirmed on ops. I’ll lock the campaign naming + UTMs and share the sheet today.

Need from folks:
- final CTA URLs for each email (console paths + docs). I want to avoid 404s if console routing is mid-change.
- suppression rules confirmation: who gets what + when we stop sending (unsub, activated, sales-assisted, etc.)

Also: deliverability check — we should throttle day 1 send volume to avoid any weirdness.

(reactions: :thumbsup: x4)

Soojin Lee: I can do a full pass on tone/claims today.

Reminder: for performance claims (latency/cost/benchmarks), we need *either* a specific blog/doc link or soften language. “Up to” / “typical” where needed.

Please flag any lines that mention specific % improvements so Ethan can sanity check.

Tessa Morgan: On creative direction for retargeting. Kenji + Alicia — can you drop your preferred visual direction for the landing page variant?

Also quick note: for dev audiences, we should keep ads super simple: snippet > abstract promise. (i.e., curl + output + a single proof point)

Kenji Nakamura: For landing/ads visual direction: code-forward. I can mock a “terminal card” style + a “dashboard latency/cost chart” style.

For console nudges: we’re keeping copy minimal in-app, but I’d like to mirror wording from emails (activation milestone language) so it feels consistent.

Alicia Perez: +1. If we’re referencing the cost dashboard in email 4/5, we should use the same name everywhere (“Latency & Cost” vs “Usage” etc). Marissa/Paula can you confirm final nav label?

Marissa Cole: Console label is “Latency & cost” in the new build (capitalization tbd, but that’s the noun phrase). Please use that.

Also: we’re feature-flagging checklist + 2 banners. If marketing copy links to specific console pages, send me the exact paths and I’ll validate against the new routing.

Paula Mendes: Instrumentation note: we’re standardizing activation events this sprint.

Primary milestone we’re leaning toward for activation metric: `first_request_success` (first 2xx completion).
Secondary milestones (for deeper activation): `first_streaming_success`, `dashboard_viewed`, `billing_added`.

If email copy asks people to “try streaming”, we need to ensure the tracking is in place (so we can measure).

Ethan Wallace: I can support benchmark proof points for retargeting + email #2.

Two safe options right now:
- “Verified performance profiles” + link to docs page
- “Benchmarks on real production workloads” + link to the blog post w/ methodology

Avoid hard numbers unless we’re citing the specific benchmark page.

Ben Carter: Awesome. Action items:

Email sequence
- Soojin: tone/claims pass today, comments in doc by 3pm PT
- Tyler: suppression + throttle proposal + deliverability checklist in tracker by EOD
- Ben: incorporate changes + push “copy lock” by Fri EOD

Retargeting
- Tessa + Kenji + Alicia: 2-3 creative directions by Mon noon
- Ethan: provide approved proof points + links by Fri
- Tyler: audiences + UTMs ready by Tue (so we can launch Week 1)

Console nudges (marketing dependencies)
- Marissa/Paula: final console route URLs for checklist + latency/cost dashboard by Fri
- Ben/Soojin: align activation wording across emails + banners (“first successful request” etc.) by Fri

If anything slips, we’ll cut scope rather than delay launch.

Avery Johnson: Adding Sales POV: please avoid language that implies enterprise features (SLA, dedicated capacity) are included by default.

We’ve had a few inbound prospects confused by “dedicated” wording in marketing emails before. Keep it Hosted API / self-serve oriented, and we can add a “Need Dedicated/VPC?” link at the bottom.

(reactions: :+1: x5)

Soojin Lee: Got it. I’ll add a single optional footer line for higher-intent users (“Need VPC/dedicated?”) pointing to a generic contact route, no big promises.

Tyler Benson: For suppression rules: proposing
- stop emails immediately on unsubscribe
- stop the “quickstart” and beyond once `first_request_success` fires
- separate troubleshooting email only if we see `first_request_error` >=2 within 24h (if we can do it cleanly)

Paula — can we reliably gate on error events in time for Week 1, or is that Week 2?

Paula Mendes: Week 1 gating on error count might be tight. We can do it, but higher QA risk.

Suggest: ship v1 with basic suppression on `first_request_success` + unsub only.
Then Week 2 iterate w/ error-triggered troubleshooting email once ENG confirms event properties are clean.

Ben Carter: Agree. Let’s do that. Week 1 = simple + safe.

For Week 1 troubleshooting email, we’ll send it on a time delay (e.g., 24h after signup) if no `first_request_success`.
Week 2 = smarter triggers.

Tessa Morgan: Works for me. Also +1 to cutting scope over pushing launch.

Kenji/Alicia — I’ll DM you re: creative review time. Let’s do a 30 min async-friendly review Mon morning.

Kenji Nakamura: 👍 I’ll post two mock directions in the creative brief doc by end of day tomorrow.

Alicia Perez: I’ll add landing page hierarchy notes (quickstart above fold, benchmarks + troubleshooting below). Also will align naming w/ “Latency & cost”.

Ben Carter: Perfect. I’ll update the tracker w/ the above owners + deadlines and post in #general once it’s finalized.

(reactions: :white_check_mark: x7)
